current_state_challenges.challenge: Eligibility checks against the 2km-of-asset rule are manual, run against a separate mapping tool with no boundary layer in the CRM; this accounts for an estimated 40% of eligibility disputes.
current_state_challenges.note: Direct quote, 12 Jun 2026 interview: 'forty percent of our eligibility disputes are on that line.'

current_state_challenges.challenge: No integration between Salesforce and SAP for vendor/payment setup; recipients are set up twice, and an estimated 1/3 of applications bounce on entity-name mismatches between the applicant-entered name and the ATO/ABN register.
Panel scores are editable in Salesforce after the panel meeting with no change history — a field overwrite destroys the prior value, so a post-decision adjustment leaves no trace.

The 'special project' exception to the 2-year re-application rule has no formal definition; it is tracked only in the Head of Communications' personal, unshared document and was applied inconsistently by an acting director during her leave.
Payment-gateway outcomes (settled/failed) do not flow back to Salesforce; a case can show 'Funded' for weeks after a payment has actually bounced.

Audit-report follow-up relies on a manual calendar reminder and a monthly report; an estimated 20% of audit reports are late or missing, and a recent compliance review could not fully account for 5 years of audit status.
current_state_challenges.note: 20% figure is Rachel's estimate, not system-verified. 5-years figure is a direct quote, 12 Jun 2026 interview: Senior Advisor 'spent three days pulling grant history for every grant in the last five years... we still had gaps that we couldn't explain.'

current_state_challenges.challenge: 5 of 11 approval-panel members lack Salesforce logins and score via spreadsheet; scores are manually transcribed into the CRM before each panel meeting, costing an estimated 40 hours/year.
Application volume has grown roughly 8x since 2019 (50/yr to ~400/yr) and the board has approved a further ~2.5x increase to ~1,000/yr by 2028, with no process maturity change to match.

business_impacts.impact: No defensible record exists for special-project overrides or panel-scoring decisions, creating regulatory and reputational exposure (anticipated Senate estimates scrutiny; two missed ministerial SLAs, one escalated to the CEO).
End-to-end disbursement for large grants takes 6-8 weeks against a recipient expectation of about a week, spending the goodwill built by approving the grant on payment-processing friction.

Manual panel-score transcription costs an estimated 40 hrs/year; MP-escalation briefing notes are manually reassembled from case history across multiple Salesforce screens for every constituent complaint, with no reusable case-summary template.

Community Marketing Leads are already straining at current volume (two on medical leave during last year's spike); the process has no slack to absorb the board-approved growth to 1,000 applications/year.
business_impacts.note: Direct quote, 12 Jun 2026 interview: 'Two of them were on medical leave by April.'

industry_context.summary: Northwind Grid operates its community grant program under increasing regulator scrutiny of how it disburses funds near its infrastructure -- a social-licence pressure specific to a state-owned utility rather than a competitive dynamic.
trends: General pattern across Australian network utilities of community-benefit-sharing programs tied to infrastructure proximity, under growing governance and audit-trail expectations -- unverified against a primary regulatory source this session.
regulatory_factors: Regulator has explicitly asked for 'evidence of monitoring' on audit-report follow-up; the organisation could not fully account for 5 years of status.
Potential Senate estimates exposure on the basis for funding decisions.

Removes the ~40 hours/year spent moving spreadsheet scores into the CRM before each panel meeting.

value_drivers.driver: Defensible audit trail for overrides and scores
value_drivers.description: Closes the specific compliance gap the regulator has already flagged in writing, and gives Rachel an answerable record for special-project decisions.
Replaces a 3-week discovery lag (recipient calls to report a bounced payment) with a status Salesforce already knows.

value_drivers.driver: A proper review workspace for external panellists
value_drivers.description: Replaces the spreadsheet-and-manual-transcription workaround for the 5 of 11 panellists without Salesforce logins.

strategic_priorities.rationale: Rachel's #1 stated priority and the single highest-cost fix: 3+ weeks of disbursement delay and ~1/3 of applications bouncing on entity-name mismatches.
Closes the specific compliance gap the regulator has already called out in writing; the current manual process cannot answer 'evidence of monitoring' requests.
A compliance and fairness requirement with no technical blocker to solving it -- the cheapest fix to deliver real governance value.

strategic_priorities.priority: Give external panellists a proper review workspace
strategic_priorities.rationale: Replaces the spreadsheet workaround for the 5 of 11 panellists without Salesforce logins, removing the manual transcription step entirely.

transformation_strategy.vision_statement: By the time the Community Care Fund reaches 1,000 applications a year, every eligibility decision, panel score, and audit follow-up is defensible on demand -- and a recipient gets paid without the SAP paperwork round-trip that costs weeks today.

strategic_objectives.success_criteria: Entity name and bank details are validated once in Salesforce and flow to SAP without manual re-entry; the mismatch bounce-back rate drops from ~1/3 toward zero.
The system tracks the 2-year due date per grant, chases the recipient automatically, and escalates to a CML and then to Rachel on schedule -- no manual calendar reminder.
Every score change is logged with who changed it and when; no field overwrite destroys a prior value.
All 11 panellists score through one system; the manual spreadsheet-transcription step is gone.
No manual bottleneck that broke at 400 applications/year (CML triage, panel-score entry, audit chasing) is still manual at 1,000/year.

principles.principle: Every funding decision leaves a record
principles.rationale: Eligibility outcomes, special-project exceptions, and panel scores are logged with reasoning, not just an outcome -- directly answers the regulator's 'evidence of monitoring' ask.

principles.principle: External reviewers work inside the platform
principles.rationale: No spreadsheet round-trips for people without a Salesforce seat; licensing exists for exactly this pattern.

principles.principle: Fix the system, not just the policy
principles.rationale: Salesforce builds the enforcement and audit structure; Rachel and Legal own defining the 'special project' policy itself -- the client's explicit choice.
Lean on standard Salesforce grantmaking patterns rather than bespoke build, consistent with the platform-health recommendations already on file for this org.

business_case.why_salesforce: The Community Care Fund already runs on Salesforce, so this extends a live platform rather than introducing a new one. The three priority fixes map to standard, proven patterns: a validated Salesforce-to-SAP data exchange for vendor setup, field history tracking for tamper-evident panel scoring, and an Experience Cloud reviewer workspace with login-based licensing for the external panellists who currently work from a spreadsheet.
business_case.why_now: The board has already approved doubling fund volume by 2028, and the current manual processes are failing at today's lower volume -- two ministerial deadlines were missed, and the regulator has already flagged the audit-tracking gap in writing. Every quarter without a defensible special-project and panel-scoring record is a quarter the organisation can't yet answer a Senate estimates question.

expected_outcomes.outcome: Shorter disbursement cycle time by removing the duplicate SAP vendor-setup round-trip
Audit-report compliance demonstrable on demand instead of requiring a multi-day manual reconstruction
Panel-scoring data integrity enforced by the platform rather than personal diligence
External panellists score directly in the system, eliminating the annual manual-transcription effort
